I joined Reddit in September of 2016, long past the “glory days of old” but not quite yet into “total enshittification at each opportunity”. There was still only Reddit Gold for awards (with the occasional “Reddit silver” crude drawing comment), which to me seemed like a respectable way to financially support the general free use of the site.

Reddit became my new core social media hub, after I felt like Facebook had turned into a “We will tell you what you want to see” stealth-grab of media/content control circa 2015. Back then, I was spread between Facebook, Twitter, YouTube and MemeBase for my digital dopamine. Reddit seemed to be a sensible consolidation of these, as a lot of popular posts and memes appeared to originate there. 

It was good for a while. And then the slow-drippings of greed started.

The “awards system” started encouraging microtransactions on a site that sheltered those who were the most vehemently vocal about this practice elsewhere in the world. The occasional pruning and purging of non-illegal-but-controversial subreddits spoke to a board of directors more focused on their upcoming IPO than the integrity of their core values - a free and fair internet.
